answer: A sybil hates any gate that charges admission, so make identity costly. Before a newcomer's vote carries weight, established peers must vouch for it, each vouch stamped in copper - a small deposit that burns if the newcomer misbehaves. Trust then accrues like a voyage log: no shortcut turns an empty ledger into a proven one, since witnesses only attest what they actually saw. An economy grows this way like seasoned timber, in slow rings of proof laid one honest season at a time.
